subject: ventures/quick-pick-survey
professional: a survey methodologist / psychometrician who fits paired-comparison (Bradley-Terry, Thurstone) models, with a full-stack engineer reviewing the Next.js and Prisma code

evidence.correctness: Ran: npm ci, prisma generate, then a throwaway vitest file (deleted afterwards) dumping outputs of the real code, compared with an independent Python implementation written from Glickman's 2012 paper (bisection for the volatility root, not the Illinois algorithm the code uses; numpy). (1-3) updateGlicko on three single-game cases (1500/200/.06 beats 1400/30; 1700/80/.05 draws 1450/120/.07; 1300/350 loses to 1500/350): rating, RD and volatility agree to about 1e-9 (e.g. 1563.5641943 vs 1563.5641943, RD 175.40265594 vs 175.40265594). My implementation also reproduces the paper's own example (1464.05 / 151.52 / 0.05999). (4) groupRanking.pool, DerSimonian-Laird on four respondents: rating 1515.55229059, se 47.29128804, tau 34.68695503, identical to 8+ digits. (5) conjoint.fitConjointModel, Davidson tie-extended BT, 10 hand-made rows, 2 features, ridge 0.08: params [3.60883406, 1.38913608], nu 0.97511211, penalised logLik -6.41536498 versus an independent gradient-descent MLE [3.60883402, 1.38913606], 0.97511210, -6.41536498. Not recomputed: pairing/selection, couples comparison, results report, admin routes (integration tests need Postgres, not run). Outputs I checked are right; the open question is the pooled SE (see domain).
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked: Glicko-2 per-respondent ratings (works, above); Davidson BT conjoint fit (works); admin-built survey with 3-60 options and pooled ranking with CSV (ranking.integration.test.ts and groupRanking unit tests exist; route code read, integration suite not run for want of Postgres); couples compare route and perspectives (code and tests present, not run live); live page https://marisstella.app/quick-pick-survey/ returns HTTP 200; every API route has a test (README claim; test files seen for admin, couple, feedback, auth). Honest self-reports held up: the README says CI has never run, VENTURE.yaml says stage prototype, hypotheses untested, production link null. Grep for TODO/FIXME in src, scripts and prisma found none. Not verified: Vercel one-click deploy end to end, page components (README admits less coverage).
evidence.verification: Ran: npx vitest run (default config), 47 files, 349 tests, all pass, but 576 s wall time (three simulation files dominate). tsc --noEmit exit 0; eslint clean. Seeded three mutations: (a) groupRanking.pool, DerSimonian-Laird scale c = sw - sum(w^2)/sw changed to sw + sum(w^2)/sw: groupRanking.test.ts 12/12 still passed (SURVIVED; the full suite was not run for this one, so another file might catch it). (b) glicko2.g(): divisor (PI*PI) changed to (PI): glicko2.test.ts 11/11 still passed; the full suite caught it in 4 tests, all slow simulation tests (infoGainPairing, pairing, pooling simulations), none a unit test. (c) conjoint outcomeLogProbs tie term dc/2 changed to dc/3: conjoint.test.ts 11/11 passed (SURVIVED, file only). Cause for (b): the file's headline test, described as 'the reference worked example ... the test that catches it', asserts only 1400 < rating < 1500 and rd < 200 after the paper's three games, not 1464.06 / 151.52. All edits reverted; git diff for the subject is empty.
evidence.craft: Read glicko2.ts (146 lines), groupRanking.ts (164), conjoint.ts (292), plus tests glicko2.test.ts and the README, llms.txt, VENTURE.yaml, site/index.html. Code is clean: typed, commented with the reason, log-space softmax, backtracking line search, formula-injection defusing in CSV, non-convergence flagged rather than hidden, a tsc and eslint pass with no output. Defects: numeric finite-difference gradient and Hessian in conjoint.ts (fine at n<=8 but slow and approximate; Hessian near-singular guard adds 1e-8 silently); invertMatrix silently perturbs a singular matrix; llms.txt has two '## Pages' sections and links the old github.io page; full test suite takes about ten minutes, so the documented 'npm run verify' gate is costly to run.
evidence.claims: Checked: README disclaimer and no-warranty text present (also site/index.html); 'ratings stored per respondent' backed by schema and participantRatings; 'every API route now has a test' backed by test files; 'CI has never run' honest. Not backed or wrong: README, src/lib/glicko2.ts and src/app/vs-typeform/page.tsx say Glicko-2 is 'the system chess.com's ratings are built on'. To my knowledge chess.com uses the original Glicko system and Lichess uses Glicko-2; I did not fetch a source in this session, so treat this as an unverified marketing claim about a third party that a reader cannot check from the repo. glicko2.test.ts calls its own loose test 'the test that catches it', which is overstated (mutation b). llms.txt live-page link points to the superseded github.io address while README uses marisstella.app.
evidence.fitness: Job: a team lead wants to rank 10 options by pairwise votes from colleagues. Walked through by code reading and docs: deploy needs a Vercel account, a Postgres store and two secrets, create survey via admin POST or UI, share /s/<slug>, read pooled ranking with intervals and rank ranges, CSV export. The coverage() advice (thin options, shorten list) is a genuinely useful touch. Gaps: not run end to end with a database in this audit; CONVERGENCE.md itself says a usable ranking needs about 5N answers per survey, so a small panel on a long list yields wide, tied ranks; no hosted instance, so a non-technical user cannot start; VENTURE.yaml shows no external user, customers null, usage unmeasured.
evidence.domain: A paired-comparison methodologist would first ask why a time-varying skill model (Glicko-2, built for players whose strength changes, with a volatility term that inflates RD after surprising answers) is used for static preferences, and would expect a Bradley-Terry / Thurstone MLE or Bayesian fit with the likelihood over all answers. The sequential one-game-per-period update is order dependent (the same answers in a different order give a different ranking); the app's own ConjointFit (Davidson BT with Wald intervals) shows the author knows the better route. Pooling across respondents treats each Glicko RD as a standard error and applies DerSimonian-Laird random effects: sensible, honest about disagreement, but RD is a heuristic posterior, so the 95% interval is approximate (the repo has a seeded coverage test and STATISTICAL-INTEGRITY.md that states limits). The Davidson tie extension and ridge prior are textbook. Departures are documented, not hidden, but a practitioner would not sign off on the discrete-item interval as a confidence interval without a coverage study on the real update rule.

defects.what: Core-logic mutations survive the unit tests: the Glicko-2 g() constant change is caught only by the slow simulation suites, and the DerSimonian-Laird scale and Davidson tie-term mutations survived their own test files. The test billed as the reference check asserts only bounds, not 1464.06 / 151.52.

Marketing and README state that chess.com's ratings are built on Glicko-2; to my knowledge chess.com uses the original Glicko (Lichess uses Glicko-2). No source in the repo. Unverified claim about a third party, repeated on a public page.

A time-varying rating model with sequential single-game updates (order dependent) is used for static preferences; the pooled interval treats RD as a standard error. Documented, but the 95% label is not validated against the real update rule.
llms.txt has a duplicate '## Pages' heading and links the old github.io live page rather than marisstella.app.
Default test suite takes about 576 s because simulation tests run in the same config as unit tests; a documented pre-commit gate that slow invites skipping.

verdict: Finished but not at the bar. Everything I recomputed (Glicko-2 on three cases, the paper's example, the random-effects pool, the Davidson BT fit) is right to 8 or more digits, the typecheck and lint are clean, and the project is unusually honest about its own gaps (CI never ran, prototype stage, no users). It misses the bar on three counts: tests do not protect the core numbers (three seeded mutations survived their unit files, and the one that was caught fell to a ten-minute simulation, not to the 'reference' test, which only checks bounds); a public page and the README attribute Glicko-2 to chess.com without a source and probably wrongly; and a paired-comparison methodologist would question a volatility-driven, order-dependent rating model as the engine for static preferences and would want a coverage study before calling the intervals 95%. Fitness is unproven: no hosted instance, no external user, and the integration suite needing Postgres was not run here. The most useful small fix is to pin 1464.06 / 151.52 (and one single-game vector) in glicko2.test.ts and add exact-value tests for pool() and the Davidson tie term.
